drills.q: What does 'autoregressive' mean for a language model, precisely?
drills.a: The model factorizes joint sequence probability as a product of conditionals, each token conditioned only on prior tokens: p(x_1..x_n) = prod p(x_t|x_<t). Trained to maximize this likelihood; at inference samples left-to-right, each new token conditioned on everything generated so far.

drills.q: Why is teacher forcing used instead of feeding the model's own predictions during training?
drills.a: Teacher forcing conditions position t's prediction on the TRUE prefix from the dataset, so every position's loss can be computed independently within one parallel forward pass -- no position waits on another's output. This is what makes trillion-token pretraining computationally tractable, at the cost of a train/inference distribution mismatch (exposure bias).

drills.q: Define exposure bias and its observable production symptom.
drills.a: Mismatch between training (true-prefix conditioning) and inference (self-generated-prefix conditioning). Symptom: compounding degradation over long free-running generations -- quality holds early, one error shifts context out-of-distribution, everything after is affected -- while teacher-forced held-out perplexity can look completely normal.

drills.q: Why can't a causal Transformer's inference forward pass work the same way as its training forward pass?
drills.a: At training time the whole sequence is already known, so one masked pass computes all positions. At inference, future tokens don't exist yet -- they ARE what's being generated -- so generation must proceed sequentially: generate token t, append it, then compute token t+1. Training is parallel; generation is inherently sequential.

drills.q: A model writes a great first paragraph then drifts into repetitive, off-topic text by paragraph four. Walk through the diagnosis.
drills.a: Check if it's length-dependent (shorter targets avoid it -- consistent with exposure bias); check positional-encoding extrapolation (is total length near/past trained context length); check decoding config (greedy/low-temperature is more prone to repetition loops once context is slightly off) before concluding it's exposure bias specifically.

drills.q: Derive the autoregressive training loss and explain what 'the loss decomposes over positions' buys operationally.
drills.a: L(theta) = -sum_t log p_theta(x_t | x_<t). Each term depends only on the TRUE prefix, so all n terms compute from one forward pass through a causally-masked network -- one GPU pass yields n supervised signals per sequence, not one.

drills.q: What is multi-token prediction and how does it relate to teacher forcing and exposure bias?
drills.a: DeepSeek-V3/Meta 2024 technique: auxiliary heads predict several future tokens per position, still fully teacher-forced (all targets are true tokens). Gives denser pretraining signal and implicit lookahead pressure, but does NOT eliminate exposure bias -- generation is still one token at a time at inference.

drills.q: Explain scheduled sampling and why it's rarely used at LLM pretraining scale today.
drills.a: Bengio 2015: feed the model's own sampled prediction instead of ground truth during training, annealed up over time, directly targeting exposure bias. But it reintroduces a sequential dependency (input at t may need position t-1's sampled output), breaking the parallel-pass property that makes trillion-token teacher-forced pretraining affordable -- RLHF/DPO/GRPO achieve a similar effect as a smaller post-training stage instead.

drills.q: Why does RL-based post-training (GRPO/RLVR) matter specifically for reasoning models in the context of exposure bias?
drills.a: Chain-of-thought traces are long; one wrong intermediate step compounds into a wrong final answer -- the exposure-bias failure shape. GRPO/RLVR trains on full autoregressive rollouts scored against verifiable outcomes, so gradient signal reflects the model's own compounding behavior, unlike teacher-forced pretraining which never sees self-generated chains.

drills.q: Design an evaluation protocol to catch an exposure-bias regression before shipping a model fine-tuned for long-form report generation.
drills.a: Don't rely solely on teacher-forced perplexity. Add: free-running generation at production-representative lengths scored for late-generation quality; a length-stratified eval tracking quality vs. position within generation (watch for a cliff); self-consistency checks across repeated generations from the same prompt. Set a concrete threshold, e.g. quality at the last quartile must not drop more than X% versus the first quartile.
